_README: Single source of the book's structure; the build is driven ENTIRELY by this file. Chapter ids start with 'ch'. A chapter is treated as translated once out/<id>_reading.md exists. Cite the book's own PRINTED FOLIO in notes, never the PDF page. This book is an ANTHOLOGY of memoir/reminiscence articles by many contributors, compiled by the Shanghai CPPCC's historical-materials committee; each 'chapter' below is one article (or a front-matter/appendix piece), modelled as a chapter so the builder gives it its own spine document. Article bylines are carried in the reading text, not in this file. Internal numbered sections (一、二、...) exist in some articles; they are captured per batch as each article is OCR'd, since the printed TOC lists only article-level entries and there are no usable PDF bookmarks below that level.

description: An annotated English translation of volume 54 of the Shanghai Selected Historical and Cultural Materials series (1986): twenty-six memoirs and studies on the secret-society gangs that ran the Shanghai underworld from the late Qing to 1949. Contributors who knew the gangs from the inside — a labour organizer, a French Concession detective, household stewards, sworn brothers and family — reconstruct the Green Gang and the Hongmen, the rise of the 'three big bosses' Huang Jinrong, Du Yuesheng and Zhang Xiaolin, and their entanglement with warlords, the concessions, the Nationalist secret service and the Communist underground. Compiled by the Shanghai CPPCC's committee on historical materials, with a preface by the historian Wei Jianyou and a contribution by Zhu Xuefan, who also inscribed the title.
subjects: BIOGRAPHY & AUTOBIOGRAPHY / Cultural, Ethnic & Regional / Asian
translator_note: This is an English translation of 旧上海的帮会 (The Gangs of Old Shanghai), volume 54 of the series Selected Historical and Cultural Materials of Shanghai (上海文史资料选辑), published by the Shanghai People's Publishing House in August 1986. It was translated from an image-only scan with no digital text layer; the Chinese text was recovered by optical character recognition and verified against the page images.

The book is not by a single author. It is an anthology of twenty-six memoirs, oral histories and short studies, compiled by the Committee on Cultural and Historical Materials of the Shanghai Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference. Some pieces are old manuscripts the committee had held unpublished; some are reprinted from other publications; many were freshly solicited from people who had known the gangs at first hand or belonged to them. Each article's contributor (and, for the oral histories, the person who took it down) is named at its head, exactly as in the original. Zhu Xuefan, then a vice-chairman of the National People's Congress Standing Committee and himself a veteran of the gang-ridden Shanghai labour movement, contributed the opening article and brushed the title on the cover; the preface is by Wei Jianyou, a professor of history at Shanghai Normal University.

The editors' own note warns that the contributors' recollections sometimes disagree, that some could not be fully checked, and that names and usages were left as each writer gave them rather than forced into uniformity. This translation keeps that honesty: where the source contradicts itself or the historical record, the text is rendered as printed and the discrepancy is footnoted, never silently repaired. Footnotes supply the people, places, institutions and customs a reader without a background in modern Chinese history would miss, and say whether the book's claims are corroborated, uncorroborated, or contradicted by outside scholarship. Chinese names use pinyin except where an older English form is conventional; damaged or uncertain readings are flagged in the notes. Passages that could not be read from the scan are marked rather than guessed at.
source_note: Image-only PDF scan, 391 pages, no text layer (producer: FreePic2Pdf). Cover bears a library seal; title page carries an accession number (124054) and a Shandong Normal University library stamp. Body is simplified Chinese, horizontal. Printed-to-PDF offset is a constant 9 (printed = pdf - 9) from the body's first page to the last, verified at multiple anchors. Front matter (editorial note, preface, table of contents) runs its own short sequences ahead of the body.
